suppress.notes:
spring-boot-mongodb-4.1.1.jar and spring-boot-starter-mongodb-4.1.1.jar (two different Spring Boot 4 MongoDB glue artifacts -- the autoconfiguration module and its own thin starter POM wrapper, respectively; a real CI re-run surfaced the starter POM's own matches separately from the autoconfig module's, already covered below, so this entry's packageUrl regex now covers both rather than adding a near-duplicate suppress block) are each being matched against two unrelated products purely because their artifactId contains "mongodb" and their version happens to be "4.1.1" (which is this project's SPRING BOOT release version, not any real external product's version):
- cpe:2.3:a:mongodb:mongodb:4.1.1 (the actual MongoDB DATABASE SERVER, version 4.1.1) -- CVE-2025-14847 ("MongoBleed", a critical uninitialized-memory-disclosure bug in the MongoDB server's own zlib handling, confirmed via Tenable/Wiz/Unit42 advisories) and CVE-2021-32036 (confirmed via MITRE/db.gcve.eu to be a real MongoDB 5.0.3 server bug) are both vulnerabilities IN THE MONGODB SERVER PROCESS ITSELF. This project does not ship or run a MongoDB server -- it connects to one over the wire via the Java driver, exactly the boundary these two CVEs live on the other side of. - cpe:2.3:a:vmware:spring_boot:4.1.1 (a generic "Spring Boot" vendor/product CPE entry, which this jar's OWN groupId:artifactId:version already gets checked against correctly elsewhere in this same report via its real packageUrl) is a duplicate, broader match adding no real additional finding beyond what the rest of this report already covers.
CVE-2026-9753 (confirmed via SentinelOne/Threat Radar to be CWE-1287, "MongoDB Aggregation Pipeline DoS Vulnerability" against "MongoDB MongoDB Server") is the same server-side pattern as CVE-2025-14847 above, not applicable to this client-side glue module.

spring-boot-data-mongodb-4.1.1.jar -- the same Spring Boot 4 auto-configuration glue module/version-coincidence pattern as spring-boot-mongodb above (see that suppress entry's own notes for the shared CVE-2025-14847/CVE-2026-9753/CVE-2021-32036/CVE-2014-8180 reasoning, all server-side MongoDB CVEs misattributed to this client-side jar via its coincidental "4.1.1" version number).
CVE-2026-41717 ("Spring Data MongoDB -- SpEL Expression Injection via Annotated Query Parameter Binding") and CVE-2026-41696 ("insufficient validation of the bound parameter" in regex parameter binding) are individually confirmed, genuinely real Spring Data MongoDB CVEs (spring.io's own security advisories, not a false product match) -- but both have a confirmed affected range of 5.0.0-5.0.5 / 4.5.0-4.5.11 / 4.4.0-4.4.14 / 4.0.0-4.3.16 / 3.4.19-and-earlier, fixed in 5.0.6+. This project's REAL spring-data-mongodb dependency (confirmed directly in the same CI run's own Maven dependency resolution log: org/springframework/data/spring-data-mongodb/5.1.1/spring-data-mongodb-5.1.1.jar) is 5.1.1 -- past the fixed version, not affected. The flagged "4.1.1" is spring-boot-data-mongodb's own version (= this project's Spring Boot release), which coincidentally falls inside the vulnerable 4.0.0-4.3.16 range for the DIFFERENT, real spring-data-mongodb artifact -- the exact version-coincidence CPE confusion this suppression file's own header describes.

protobuf-java-4.35.1.jar (pulled in transitively via spring-boot-starter-opentelemetry -> opentelemetry-exporter-otlp -> opentelemetry-proto, for OTLP's binary wire-format encoding -- see pom.xml's own Spring Boot 4 migration comment for why this project depends on spring-boot-starter-opentelemetry at all) is flagged for CVE-2026-0994. Confirmed via osv.dev's own advisory: this CVE is a JSON-parsing recursion-depth denial-of-service bug specifically in `google.protobuf.json_format.ParseDict()` -- the PYTHON protobuf package's own pure-Python JSON glue code, not the Java artifact. NVD's CPE dictionary matches both language bindings under the same generic "google:protobuf"/"protobuf-java" product entries, a cross-ecosystem false positive OWASP Dependency-Check is known to produce. This project never uses Python, and the Java protobuf-java usage here is exclusively OpenTelemetry's binary OTLP wire format, not any untrusted-JSON-to-protobuf parsing path.

kotlin-stdlib-2.3.21.jar (pulled in transitively via spring-boot-starter-opentelemetry -> opentelemetry-exporter-otlp -> opentelemetry-exporter-sender-okhttp -> okhttp-jvm -> okio-jvm, which is partly written in Kotlin and needs kotlin-stdlib present at runtime -- see pom.xml's own Spring Boot 4 migration comment) is flagged for CVE-2026-53914, CVSS 9.8. Confirmed via JetBrains' own advisory (also cross-checked against SentinelOne's vulnerability database): this is specifically an unsafe-deserialization RCE in the KOTLIN COMPILER'S OWN BUILD CACHE subsystem -- triggered only when a Kotlin/Gradle build consumes poisoned metadata from a remote build-cache backend during compilation. It is not reachable by an application merely having the kotlin-stdlib RUNTIME jar on its classpath as a transitive dependency of a third-party library (here, okhttp/okio), with no Kotlin code of its own. This project is a plain Java/Maven build: it never invokes the Kotlin compiler, has no Gradle build-cache configuration of any kind, local or remote, and ships kotlin-stdlib only because okhttp needs it at runtime -- the vulnerable attack surface (a Kotlin build process deserializing untrusted remote build-cache entries) does not exist anywhere in this project's build or runtime.

spring-security-web-7.1.1.jar flagged for CVE-2026-47838 ("SubjectDnX509PrincipalExtractor fails to properly handle malformed X.509 certificate Common Name values, enabling user impersonation via crafted client certificates"). Confirmed via the official GitHub Security Advisory (GHSA-293q-567p-wmwq) that its own listed affected ranges are >=6.5.0,<=6.5.10 / >=6.4.0,<=6.4.13 / >=6.0.0,<=6.3.10 / >=5.8.0,<=5.8.16 / <=5.7.14, fixed in 6.5.11 -- this project's actual version, 7.1.1 (a full major line ahead of the fixed 6.5.11, part of this session's own Spring Boot 4 / Spring Framework 7 bump), falls outside every one of those ranges and already contains whatever fix 6.5.11 shipped. Same NVD CPE-matching pattern this suppression file's own header describes: a generic "spring_security" product/version match with no awareness that 7.1.1 postdates the fixed 6.5.11 release. This project also does not use X.509 client-certificate authentication anywhere (confirmed via SecurityConfig -- JWT bearer tokens are the only auth mechanism), so even a genuine finding here would have no real attack surface to reach.
